claims.explanation: NSC-663284 is a quinoline-5,8-dione that inhibits Cdc25 phosphatases and also redox-cycles to generate reactive oxygen species, so selectivity likely reflects dependence on Cdc25/CDK1-2 activity and on oxidative-stress/apoptosis buffering. Sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/RAF-pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NF1) and TP53 pathway loss, which increase reliance on Cdc25-mediated G2/M progression and lower apoptotic threshold, while resistant lines often retain wild-type-like BRAF/RAS signaling or have intact survival signaling. Features predicting sensitivity are therefore activating MAPK-pathway mutations and loss of p53/CDKN2A, with protective features being intact RB/CDK-inhibitor pathways and strong antioxidant programs.

features.basis: BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid lines are among the most killed; RAF activation increases Cdc25/CDK dependence
KRAS-mutant lung/colorectal/pancreatic lines are enriched in the sensitive set
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling and appears in multiple sensitive lines
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines and lowers apoptotic threshold to Cdc25 inhibition/ROS
CDKN2A loss removes p16/p14ARF brakes and is enriched in sensitive lines
RB1-mutant lines are overrepresented among least-affected lines, suggesting intact G1/S control is not required for survival
PTEN loss appears in several resistant lines and may buffer oxidative/apoptotic stress
ARID1A mutation is common in resistant lines, possibly reflecting chromatin-state survival programs
Cdc25A is the most potently inhibited target (Ki 29 nM) and its expression should increase drug dependence
Cdc25B is a primary target and redox-regulated by quinolinediones
Cdc25C inhibition blocks G2/M and is expected to sensitize proliferating cells
NFE2L2/KEAP1 pathway activation may protect against quinone redox-cycling ROS
